app.title: Catch that Dih!
boss.020.phase2.ansage: He's heading for the weed bed!
boss.040.phase2.ansage: A whirlpool! The current is turning!
boss.040.phase3.ansage: Light show! Follow the moving zone!
boss.060.phase2.ansage: He's ramming the ice! Chop your hole free!
boss.060.phase4.ansage: Your line is icing up – hurry!
boss.080.phase2.ansage: Flash! Trust the sound and vibration!
boss.080.phase3.ansage: Lumina pulls toward the trench floor!
boss.080.phase4.ansage: Her jaws open – every lantern flickers!
boss.100.phase3.ansage: Ignaris leaps over the jetty – lava bombs!
fish.001.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 0–8 m down (Open Water).
fish.001.lexicon: The classic. Every angler catches their first one here.
fish.001.name: Roach
fish.002.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine or cloudy skies – 2–10 m down (Open Water).
fish.002.lexicon: Striped like a tiger, but really more of a house cat.
fish.002.name: European Perch
fish.003.hint: Word is, this one bites in the evening and at night – 8–15 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.003.lexicon: Flat as a plate, slippery as soap. Hoovers up the lake bed.
fish.003.name: Common Bream
fish.004.hint: Rumour has it this one bites in the morning, and loves cloudy skies or rain – 3–15 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.004.lexicon: Also called the "doctor fish": legend says its slime heals other fish.
fish.004.name: Tench
fish.005.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 0–3 m down (Shallows).
fish.005.lexicon: People once made fake pearls from its scales. Truly dazzling!
fish.005.name: Bleak
fish.006.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day and in the evening, and loves sunshine – 0–4 m down (Shallows).
fish.006.lexicon: Red fins, golden flanks – a roach in its Sunday best.
fish.006.name: Rudd
fish.007.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 10–25 m down (Deep Hole).
fish.007.lexicon: Small, curious and always nose-down. A real sniffer dog.
fish.007.name: Gudgeon
fish.008.hint: Rumour has it this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 0–5 m down (Shallows).
fish.008.lexicon: Came from North America and simply made itself at home.
fish.008.name: Pumpkinseed
fish.009.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites in the morning and in the evening, and loves cloudy skies – 5–15 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.009.lexicon: Can live for over 50 years – and remembers every hook.
fish.009.name: Common Carp
fish.010.hint: Anglers say this one bites in the evening and at night, and loves cloudy skies or rain – 8–20 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.010.lexicon: Its eyes see so well in the dark that they shine. Torch included.
fish.010.name: Zander
fish.011.hint: Word is, this one bites at night, and loves rain or thunderstorms – 10–25 m down (Deep Hole).
fish.011.lexicon: Swims all the way to the Sargasso Sea to spawn – over 5,000 km. No satnav!
fish.011.name: European Eel
fish.012.hint: Rumour has it this one bites in the morning, and loves rain or cloudy skies – 2–8 m down (Open Water).
fish.012.lexicon: Always carries a rainbow, even when it isn't raining.
fish.012.name: Rainbow Trout
fish.013.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day, and loves rain – 0–2 m down (Shallows).
fish.013.lexicon: Half frog, half fish, all silliness. Ribbit!
fish.013.name: Lily Hopper
fish.014.hint: Anglers say this one bites in the morning and in the evening, and loves cloudy skies or rain – 3–15 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.014.lexicon: Lurks in the weeds and shoots out like an arrow.
fish.014.name: Northern Pike
fish.015.hint: Word is, this one bites at night – 15–25 m down (Deep Hole).
fish.015.lexicon: Its ancestors swam alongside the dinosaurs. It's in no hurry.
fish.015.name: Sterlet
fish.016.hint: Rumour has it this one bites in the morning, and loves rain or morning fog – 10–20 m down (Weed Bed).
fish.016.lexicon: So old she's growing a garden on her back. The snail pays no rent.
fish.016.name: Mossbeard Crucian
fish.017.hint: Only on nights without rain – then it twinkles 0–5 m down (Shallows). Especially often at full moon.
fish.017.lexicon: If you spot one, you get a wish. So says Grandpa Otto.
fish.017.name: Firefly Perch
fish.018.hint: Anglers say this one bites at night, and loves thunderstorms or rain – 15–25 m down (Deep Hole).
fish.018.lexicon: Europe's biggest freshwater fish. Said to have swallowed the odd duck – purely by accident, of course.
fish.018.name: Wels Catfish
fish.019.hint: Word is, this one bites in the morning, and loves sunshine – 0–5 m down (Shallows).
fish.019.lexicon: Someone released him from a garden pond 100 years ago. He's been blooming ever since.
fish.019.name: Cherry Blossom Koi
fish.020.hint: Barnabas is asleep. He only leaves the Deep Hole (15–25 m) at night during a thunderstorm or full moon.
fish.020.lexicon: Five lures in his jaw, zero respect for anglers. Whoever lands him becomes a legend.
fish.020.name: Old Barnabas
fish.021.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites during the day – 0–6 m down (Lagoon).
fish.021.lexicon: Lives in an anemone that stings everyone else. Best bodyguard in the world.
fish.021.name: Clown Anemonefish
fish.022.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 3–15 m down (Reef Top).
fish.022.name: Blue Tang
fish.023.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 0–8 m down (Lagoon).
fish.023.lexicon: Wears stripes like a uniform, yet never stands to attention.
fish.023.name: Humbug Damselfish
fish.024.hint: Rumour has it this one bites during the day – 5–15 m down (Reef Top).
fish.024.lexicon: Picks food out of every crack with its tweezer snout. Very tidy!
fish.024.name: Copperband Butterflyfish
fish.025.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites in the morning, and loves sunshine – 5–15 m down (Reef Top).
fish.025.lexicon: Turns coral into sand. Yes, really.
fish.025.name: Masked Parrotfish
fish.026.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day – 0–6 m down (Lagoon).
fish.026.lexicon: Guards its eggs like a drill sergeant. At ease!
fish.026.name: Indo-Pacific Sergeant
fish.027.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 10–20 m down (Reef Top).
fish.027.lexicon: Loves lying in the sand pretending it isn't there.
fish.027.name: Bluespotted Ribbontail Ray
fish.028.hint: Rumour has it this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 3–10 m down (Reef Top).
fish.028.name: Yellow Boxfish
fish.029.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites in the evening – 5–15 m down (Reef Top).
fish.029.lexicon: When it gets nervous, it gets round. Very round.
fish.029.name: White-spotted Puffer
fish.030.hint: Anglers say this one bites in the evening and at night – 10–25 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.030.lexicon: Looks like a circus tent with fins. Please don't touch – the spines are venomous!
fish.030.name: Red Lionfish
fish.031.hint: Word is, this one bites during the day – 5–15 m down (Reef Top).
fish.031.lexicon: Its dorsal fin flutters like a pennant. Always ready for a parade.
fish.031.name: Moorish Idol
fish.032.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at night – 10–25 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.032.lexicon: Cracks crabs like a nutcracker. The zebra stripes come free.
fish.032.name: Zebra Moray
fish.033.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 0–8 m down (Lagoon).
fish.033.lexicon: Smells faintly of the funfair. Please reel it in very gently!
fish.033.name: Candyfloss Seahorse
fish.034.hint: Anglers say this one bites in the morning and in the evening – 15–30 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.034.lexicon: Always grinning, even when nothing's funny. Blame the teeth.
fish.034.name: Great Barracuda
fish.035.hint: Word is, this one bites during the day – 20–35 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.035.lexicon: Curious as a puppy and big as a sofa. He just wants to say hello.
fish.035.name: Humphead Wrasse
fish.036.hint: Rumour has it this one bites in the evening – 5–12 m down (Reef Top).
fish.036.lexicon: Smaller than your thumb, more colourful than your whole paint box.
fish.036.name: Mandarinfish
fish.037.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 10–25 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.037.lexicon: When it leaps, you get a free rainbow.
fish.037.name: Prismfin
fish.038.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day, and loves sunshine – 30–50 m down (Blue Water).
fish.038.name: Sailfish
fish.039.hint: Word is, this one bites at night only during the coral bloom or tropical showers at high tide – 15–30 m down (Reef Edge).
fish.039.lexicon: A walking reef with little horns. Housemates included.
fish.039.name: Coral Dragon
fish.040.hint: The Empress only appears on full-moon nights or at high tide around sunset – out in the Blue Water (30–50 m).
fish.040.lexicon: Ruler of the reef. When she glides, even the waves hold their breath.
fish.040.name: Empress Coralina
fish.041.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 0–20 m down (Cold Water).
fish.041.lexicon: Has antifreeze in its blood and feels right at home at minus 2 °C.
fish.041.name: Polar Cod
fish.042.hint: Anglers say this one bites in the morning – 0–10 m down (Ice Hole).
fish.042.lexicon: Never travels alone. Where there's one capelin, there are a thousand more.
fish.042.name: Capelin
fish.043.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day, and loves cloudy skies – 5–20 m down (Cold Water).
fish.043.lexicon: Supposedly chats by blowing bubble toots. Even scientists giggled.
fish.043.name: Atlantic Herring
fish.044.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day – 20–45 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.044.lexicon: Looks grumpy and grunts when you lift it. Seriously.
fish.044.name: Shorthorn Sculpin
fish.045.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites in the morning, and loves snow – 0–15 m down (Cold Water).
fish.045.lexicon: Lives farther north than any other freshwater fish. Chilly? Never heard of it.
fish.045.name: Arctic Char
fish.046.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day – 20–40 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.046.lexicon: Can live past 70. It's had those goggle eyes since it was a baby.
fish.046.name: Golden Redfish
fish.047.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day, and loves snow – 0–5 m down (Ice Hole).
fish.047.lexicon: No two snowflakes are alike. Neither are these gobies.
fish.047.name: Snowflake Goby
fish.048.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at night – 20–45 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.048.lexicon: Has no red blood. No joke.
fish.048.name: Blackfin Icefish
fish.049.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day, and loves cloudy skies – 30–60 m down (Fjord Floor).
fish.049.lexicon: Has both eyes on one side. As a baby it swam just like everyone else.
fish.049.name: Atlantic Halibut
fish.050.hint: Anglers say this one bites at night – 25–50 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.050.lexicon: Looks scary, but is actually shy.
fish.050.name: Atlantic Wolffish
fish.051.hint: Word is, this one bites during the day – 10–30 m down (Cold Water).
fish.051.lexicon: Sticks to rocks with its belly. Males wear an orange belly, females blue-green – the lexicon shows both.
fish.051.name: Lumpsucker
fish.052.hint: Rumour has it this one bites in the morning, and loves rain – 5–20 m down (Cold Water).
fish.052.lexicon: Leaps up waterfalls to get home. And you complain about stairs?
fish.052.name: Atlantic Salmon
fish.053.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites in the morning only during snow – 0–15 m down (Cold Water).
fish.053.lexicon: Its fins tinkle softly when it leaps. Please do not defrost.
fish.053.name: Frostfeather Trout
fish.054.hint: Anglers say this one bites at night – 40–70 m down (Fjord Floor).
fish.054.lexicon: Lives in the coldest sea on Earth – with built-in antifreeze, of course.
fish.054.name: Antarctic Toothfish
fish.055.hint: Word is, this one bites at night, and loves the northern lights – 15–35 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.055.lexicon: The narwhal wanted to be a fish. The needlefish wanted a horn. Everyone's happy.
fish.055.name: Narwhal Needlefish
fish.056.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day only during blizzards – 30–50 m down (Iceberg Roots).
fish.056.lexicon: Jingles like a wind chime when caught. Gloves recommended.
fish.056.name: Icicle Eel
fish.057.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at night only during the northern lights – 5–25 m down (Cold Water).
fish.057.lexicon: Wears the northern lights on its skin. Torch? Doesn't need one.
fish.057.name: Aurora Neon
fish.058.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day, and loves cloudy skies or ice fog – 30–60 m down (Fjord Floor).
fish.058.lexicon: Can't decide whether he's a fish or a walrus. So he's both.
fish.058.name: Walrus Catfish
fish.059.hint: Word is, this one bites at night, and loves blizzards – 40–70 m down (Fjord Floor).
fish.059.lexicon: Where it swims, it snows. Its armour is older than some glaciers.
fish.059.name: Glacier Sturgeon
fish.060.hint: Grimbeard is in no hurry. He only rises from the Fjord Floor (50–70 m) at night during a blizzard.
fish.060.lexicon: Greenland sharks can live for over 400 years. Grimbeard stopped counting.
fish.060.name: Grimbeard, the Glacier Shark
fish.061.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 200–1,000 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.061.lexicon: Every night it rises hundreds of metres to feed and sinks again at dawn – the biggest migration on Earth.
fish.061.name: Lanternfish
fish.062.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day – 200–1,000 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.062.lexicon: The lights on its belly make it invisible from below. An invisibility cloak made of light!
fish.062.name: Silver Hatchetfish
fish.063.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 500–1,500 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.063.lexicon: Probably the most common vertebrate on Earth, and hardly anyone knows it.
fish.063.name: Bristlemouth
fish.064.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day – 600–1,200 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.064.lexicon: Down in the deep it looks perfectly normal. Only up here, without the water pressure, does it slump into a sad blob. So please don't laugh!
fish.064.name: Blobfish
fish.065.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at night – 500–2,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.065.lexicon: Its teeth don't fit in its mouth. At night it rises to 200 m to hunt.
fish.065.name: Viperfish
fish.066.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day, and loves a whale-fall feast – 1,000–4,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.066.lexicon: Tail like a rat, eyes like saucers. Loves a whale-fall feast.
fish.066.name: Grenadier
fish.067.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 1,000–2,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.067.lexicon: Blacker than night – with its own torch on its chin.
fish.067.name: Black Dragonfish
fish.068.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day – 1,000–3,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.068.lexicon: A mouth with a bit of fish attached. Gulps prey almost as big as itself.
fish.068.name: Pelican Eel
fish.069.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 2,000–5,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.069.lexicon: Looks nasty, but fits in your hand.
fish.069.name: Fangtooth
fish.070.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day, and loves a whale-fall feast – 700–3,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.070.lexicon: Swallowed a fish bigger than itself. Now what? Time for a digestive stroll.
fish.070.name: Black Swallower
fish.071.hint: Word is, this one bites at night – 600–800 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.071.lexicon: The dots at the front are its nose. The eyes are inside its head. Yes, really.
fish.071.name: Barreleye
fish.072.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day – 200–1,000 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.072.lexicon: Half jellyfish, half fish, fully charged. Careful, it crackles!
fish.072.name: Neon Jellyfin
fish.073.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day only during a bioluminescence wave – 1,000–3,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.073.lexicon: See a shoal and you're seeing shooting stars. Make a wish!
fish.073.name: Stardust Sardine
fish.074.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day – 1,000–4,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.074.lexicon: He fishes too, only better than you.
fish.074.name: Humpback Anglerfish
fish.075.hint: Word is, this one bites at night – 300–1,300 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.075.lexicon: Shoots its jaw forward like a drawer. Snap!
fish.075.name: Goblin Shark
fish.076.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day, and loves marine snow – 2,000–5,000 m down (Midnight Zone).
fish.076.lexicon: You can see right into its heart. And it beats pretty fast while you reel it in.
fish.076.name: Crystal Skull Fish
fish.077.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at night – 150–700 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.077.lexicon: Thought to have died out 66 million years ago, until one was found in 1938.
fish.077.name: Coelacanth
fish.078.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day, and loves storms – 200–1,000 m down (Twilight Zone).
fish.078.lexicon: Probably the origin of many sea-serpent legends.
fish.078.name: Giant Oarfish
fish.079.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day only during a bioluminescence wave – 4,000–6,000 m down (Abyssal Zone).
fish.079.lexicon: You only see it when it glows. And when it doesn't, it's still there.
fish.079.name: Phantom Ray
fish.080.hint: When the vents glow red, Lumina awakens – at the very bottom of the Deep-Sea Trench (6,000–11,000 m).
fish.080.lexicon: Queen of the deep. No submarine has ever seen her light and reported back.
fish.080.name: Lumina, the Abyss Lantern
fish.081.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 0–5 m down (Thermal Pools).
fish.081.lexicon: In reality it lives in just one warm water cave in Nevada, where it is critically endangered. Down here it has found a second home.
fish.081.name: Devils Hole Pupfish
fish.082.hint: Anglers say this one bites during the day – 0–8 m down (Thermal Pools).
fish.082.lexicon: In real life it swims in soda lakes over 40 °C. A hot bath? Far too chilly!
fish.082.name: Magadi Tilapia
fish.083.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day, and loves ash rain – 5–20 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.083.lexicon: Puffs little ash clouds when it flees. Sneezes included.
fish.083.name: Ash Goby
fish.084.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at night – 0–10 m down (Thermal Pools).
fish.084.lexicon: A handful of sparklers with fins. Do not keep in your pocket!
fish.084.name: Spark Darter
fish.085.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day – 10–25 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.085.lexicon: Loves snuggling between tube worms at hot vents. Cosy!
fish.085.name: Vent Eelpout
fish.086.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day, and loves an eruption – 0–10 m down (Thermal Pools).
fish.086.name: Pumice Perch
fish.087.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day – 5–20 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.087.lexicon: Smells of rotten eggs. Catch it anyway.
fish.087.name: Sulphur Carp
fish.088.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day – 20–40 m down (Crystal Caves).
fish.088.lexicon: Shines like a mirror of volcanic glass. Please don't drop it.
fish.088.name: Obsidian Scaler
fish.089.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at any time of day, and it adores crystal bait – 20–40 m down (Crystal Caves).
fish.089.lexicon: Has no eyes, yet finds every crystal bait. Can it hear the crystals sing?
fish.089.name: Crystal Cave Tetra
fish.090.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day – 40–55 m down (Magma Chamber).
fish.090.lexicon: Cool outside, glowing inside. Like a lava cake with fins.
fish.090.name: Ember Perch
fish.091.hint: Word is, this one bites at night, and loves steam fog – 10–30 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.091.lexicon: Always smiling, even when its gills are on fire. A real ray of sunshine.
fish.091.name: Salamanderfish
fish.092.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day, and loves steam fog – 5–20 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.092.lexicon: Whistles like a kettle when it puffs up. Time for a cuppa?
fish.092.name: Steam Puffer
fish.093.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at night – 40–55 m down (Magma Chamber).
fish.093.lexicon: Looks like molten lava and behaves like it. No petting!
fish.093.name: Magma Moray
fish.094.hint: Anglers say this one bites at any time of day only during an eruption – 0–15 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.094.lexicon: When it burns out, it hatches anew from its own ashes.
fish.094.name: Phoenixfin
fish.095.hint: Word is, this one bites at night – 40–60 m down (Magma Chamber).
fish.095.lexicon: Its skin looks like a lava pavement. Please don't walk on it.
fish.095.name: Basalt Catfish
fish.096.hint: Rumour has it this one bites at any time of day, and it adores crystal bait – 20–40 m down (Crystal Caves).
fish.096.lexicon: Lived 360 million years ago. Never found out it was extinct.
fish.096.name: Amethyst Placoderm
fish.097.hint: Grandpa Otto swears this one bites at night only during Rune Night, and it adores crystal bait – 20–40 m down (Crystal Caves).
fish.097.lexicon: Now it's here, now it's there. Follow it and you'll get lost – or catch it.
fish.097.name: Will-o'-Wisp Ghostfish
fish.098.hint: Anglers say this one bites at night, and loves an eruption – 0–20 m down (Sulphur Vents).
fish.098.lexicon: Swam up the lava fall and became a dragon. And what did you achieve today?
fish.098.name: Fire Dragon Koi
fish.099.hint: Word is, this one bites at any time of day only during earthquakes, and it adores crystal bait – 40–60 m down (Magma Chamber).
fish.099.name: Rock Muncher
fish.100.hint: Ignaris only awakens during a Great Eruption at night – deep in the Ember Lake (55–60 m).
fish.100.lexicon: The dragon beneath the volcano. His breath makes even lava sweat.
fish.100.name: Ignaris, the Lava Dragonfish
test.title: Test tank: {world}
world.1.name: Sunmirror Lake
world.2.name: Rainbow Reef
world.3.name: Frost Fjord
world.4.name: Glowing Deep
world.5.name: Ember Grotto
